notes.title: How would you like to see this game in the future?
notes.notes: [p][b]Greetings![/b][/p][p]Based on the demo version, tell me — how do you imagine the full version of the game? How do you see it, and what would you ideally want it to become? Things like duration, genre features: open world or linear? First-person, third-person, or maybe both? Or even isometric? More like a Soulslike, or Dark Messiah? Maybe closer to TES, Gothic, Dragon Age, or Baldur’s Gate? I’m curious to know what kind of gameplay you’d like this project to resemble.[/p][p]Do you want quests, dialogues, choices with consequences? Or do you prefer more exploration and gameplay-focused combat without too much emphasis on story? Do you want realism — like in Mordhau or Kingdom Come Deliverance — where armor has weak points and weapons interact differently with different types of protection? Or does that feel like too much complexity, and you’d prefer something more classic fantasy, intuitive, and skill/timing-based with combos?[/p][p]Personally, I have many different formats in my head for how this project could be developed, but I need your feedback to shape a clear vision.[/p][p]For example, as a fan of Fallout 2 and Wartales, one possible vision I see is this:[/p][p]You leave a city and enter a global map. In Fallout it was just a black screen with dots, but that feels outdated — I’d make it more like Wartales, but with our combat system, not turn-based but action-based. Imagine a huge world with diverse biomes — deserts, snowy peaks, something like Middle-earth or Game of Thrones’ world — with politics, complex themes, and dark fantasy. As you travel across the map, you’d encounter random events and unique locations. And when you arrive at cities, dungeons, ruins, you’d switch to first- or third-person gameplay, fighting just like in the demo.[/p][p]No party system — just one main character, like in Fallout. A big map with scripted events and points of interest, quests, and dialogues.[/p][p]What do you think of this idea?[/p][p]But this is only one possible vision. The game could also take the form of a 10-hour linear experience in the style of Dark Messiah, or become a full open-world RPG with freedom and consequences.[/p]

notes.title: Does the game need a 3rd person view?
notes.notes:
We have the opportunity to transfer the game to a new engine, but then it will be in 3rd person, and will also receive several additional features.

NPCs, dialogues, and quests will appear in the game.
Crafting weapons and armor.
there will be a completely different, more intuitive and enjoyable combat system, with different combinations and directions of attacks.
Smarter AI, for example, ranged enemies will appear.
There will also be upgrades, skills, characteristics, and more abilities.
The game will have fewer bugs and more dynamics.

In fact, a lot of things that the game is criticized for in discussions will be corrected.
But this will be a slightly different project from a gameplay point of view, the atmosphere, locations, plot, types of enemies will be preserved, but the approach to battles and exploration will change.

The only downside here is that it will take us an extra few months to complete the transfer.

I would like to know your opinion on this matter, what kind of game you would like to see.

notes.title: Dark Souls and Skyrim come together in this upcoming RPG
notes.notes:
Eldrimar is an upcoming RPG game that I am genuinely excited about, especially as someone who has long been awaiting The Elder Scrolls 6 release date. By blending the disturbingly dark setting of soulslike titles with the familiar first-person gameplay of Skyrim, Eldrimar builds itself into a unique fantasy experience. As a fan of all things medieval, especially when such elements are thrust into fantastical or magical worlds, I would definitely say that Honor Games' upcoming title is at the least, a very fascinating one.
